lease.title: Lease
lease.notFound: This lease does not exist or is not in this portfolio.
lease.breakdownHint: The sum must equal the rent.
confirm.title: Confirm
confirm.activate: The lease becomes active: its first rent call will be issued by the monthly billing. It can then only change by amendment.
confirm.notice: The notice is recorded with the end date given.
confirm.end: The lease ends: no further rent call will be issued.
confirm.close: The lease is closed for good; its guarantees can no longer change.
confirm.generate: The contract is generated from the current draft and archived; it can no longer change.
guarantee.name: Name or company name
guarantee.hidden: Guarantor data is not visible to your role.
inventory.mode.amicable: Capture it in Tenure, on site
inventory.denied: Inventories are not available to your role.
inventory.unsavedBlocks: {n} change(s) not saved: save them before moving to the next step.
inventory.editsKept: The inventory was reloaded; your unsaved meters, keys and observations are kept.
inventory.completedNext: Capture completed: have each party sign, or reopen the capture while nobody has signed.
inventory.issuedNote: This inventory is issued: it can no longer change.
inventory.check.covering-not-assessed: Floor, walls or ceiling not assessed
inventory.check.damage-unexplained: Poor or unusable without a comment or a photo
help.profile.legalName: Your name, or your company's name (SCI…), as it will appear as landlord on leases and receipts.
help.profile.address: The landlord's address, required on the lease and on receipts.
help.profile.taxId: Your 13-digit French tax number, used for form 2044. Optional.
help.profile.language: Language of the app and of your e-mails. Generated documents are always in French.
help.asset.kind: House, apartment or parking box. The kind decides which leases and diagnostics apply; it cannot change afterwards.
help.asset.address: Full address of the rented property, shown on the lease and the rent calls.
help.asset.lot: Lot number or marker (floor, door, box number) to tell apart several properties at the same address.
help.asset.surface: Living area (Boutin law) in m², two decimals at most. It appears on the lease and is used for rent control.
help.asset.parent: Attach the box to the dwelling it goes with, to let them together. Leave “None” for a box let on its own.
help.asset.furnished: Tick if the dwelling is furnished (minimum list of the 2015 decree): the lease will be a furnished lease.
help.asset.dpe: Class of the latest energy performance diagnostic (A to G). A class too low blocks letting.
help.asset.controlledZone: Tick only if the town caps rent levels by prefectoral order (Paris, Lyon, Lille, the city of Montpellier…): the rent will be capped at the maximum reference rent. A neighbouring town may be in a tense area without a cap.
help.asset.tenseZone: Tick if the town is in a zone tendue (large urban areas listed by decree; check with the service-public.fr simulator). A new rent there may not exceed the previous tenant’s rent revised by IRL, and the lease states that rent. A rent-control area is always a tense area.
help.asset.rentZone: Zone of the prefectoral order where the property lies, e.g. “Lyon-3”.
help.asset.rentCategory: Category of the order (rooms, construction period, furnished or not), e.g. “T2 before 1946”.
help.asset.acquiredOn: Purchase date of the property. Optional; used for tax.
help.asset.acquisition: Purchase price, with costs if you wish. Optional; used for tax.
help.diag.kind: The diagnostic concerned. Those required for a dwelling show as blockers on the lease while missing.
help.diag.notRequired: Tick if this diagnostic is not required for this property (e.g. no gas installation), and say why.
help.diag.reason: Why the diagnostic is not required; it is kept on file.
help.diag.doneOn: Date the report was made, as written on it.
help.diag.validUntil: End of validity if the report states one. Tenure keeps the earlier of this date and the diagnostic's legal validity, from the legal parameters.
help.diag.result: For a DPE, the energy class (A to G). For the others, the result in a few words (e.g. “no asbestos”).
help.tenant.names: Full name of each tenant, one per line, as they will appear on the lease.
help.tenant.email: Where rent calls and receipts are sent. Optional, but nothing is e-mailed without it.
help.tenant.phone: A number to reach the tenant. Optional.
help.tenant.language: Language of the e-mails sent to the tenant. Documents stay in French.
help.tenant.occupation: Student or apprentice: a surety stays possible alongside a rent insurance (1989 law, art. 22-1).
help.lease.kind: Unfurnished, furnished, mobility lease (reserved for some tenants, no deposit) or a parking box. The proposed term and deposit follow the kind.
help.lease.mobilityReason: The mobility lease is reserved for a tenant in training, studies, internship, apprenticeship, civic service, job transfer or a temporary assignment.
help.lease.assets: The properties this lease lets: for example an apartment and its box.
help.lease.tenants: The signing tenants. They are jointly liable for the rent. Create one with the button on the right.
help.lease.startOn: Date the lease takes effect. Proposed as the 1st of next month.
help.lease.term: Lease term in months. Proposed from the legal term of the lease kind; you may agree a longer one.
help.lease.termNone: No legal term is known for this kind: enter the agreed term.
help.lease.rent: Monthly rent excluding charges, in euros. In a rent-control area it is checked against the maximum reference rent.
help.lease.provision: Monthly provision for recoverable charges, settled each year against the actual costs.
help.lease.deposit: Proposed at the legal cap for the lease kind (rent excluding charges × the allowed number of months). You may ask for less.
help.lease.dueDay: Day of the month the rent is due, between 1 and 28. The 1st is the usual choice; the reminder follows a few days later.
help.lease.irlQuarter: Quarter of the rent reference index (IRL) used as the base for the yearly revision. Proposed as the latest quarter published by INSEE.
help.lease.irlValue: Value of the IRL for that quarter, e.g. 145.47. Filled in with the proposed quarter.
help.lease.revisionMonth: Month the rent is revised each year by the IRL. Proposed as the lease's anniversary month.
help.lease.exemption: In a tense area, a new rent above the previous rent revised by IRL is only allowed after improvement works or for a manifestly under-valued rent. The exemption never lifts a rent-control cap.
help.lease.clauses: Vetted special clauses the contract will carry. Unfair clauses are not offered.
help.lease.breakdown: With several properties, give each one's share of the rent: it is used for tax and rent control.
help.lease.noticeEnd: Date the lease will end, once the legal notice period runs out; it depends on who gives notice, the lease kind and the area.
help.guarantee.kind: Deposit, a person's surety, Visale (Action Logement) or rent insurance. A surety cannot be combined with an insurance, except for a student or apprentice tenant.
help.guarantee.status: Deposit: held while you keep it, settled once returned. Other guarantees: valid or expired.
help.guarantee.amount: Amount received. Proposed as the deposit set by the lease.
help.guarantee.name: Name of the person (or company) standing as surety.
help.guarantee.address: The surety's address, shown on the surety act.
help.guarantee.legalPerson: Tick if the surety is a company rather than a person.
help.guarantee.solidary: Joint and several: you can claim from the surety without first pursuing the tenant. This is the usual form.
help.guarantee.visa: Number of the Visale visa issued to the tenant by Action Logement.
help.guarantee.validFrom: Start of the guarantee's validity. Proposed as the lease start date.
help.guarantee.validTo: End of validity, if the guarantee has one. Leave empty for the lease's duration.
help.inventory.kind: The entry inventory is required before activating the lease; the exit one is done when the tenant leaves.
help.inventory.doneOn: Date of the inventory. Proposed as the lease start for entry, its end for exit.
help.inventory.file: The inventory signed by both parties, as a PDF. It is scanned, then archived.
help.inventory.mode: Captured in Tenure, the inventory starts from the asset's layout, is filled in on site room by room, then Tenure issues the document. Otherwise, upload the signed PDF of an inventory made elsewhere.
help.capture: Assess each item on the five-level scale: every change is saved at once. A poor or unusable item needs a comment or a photo.
help.capture.doneOn: The day the inventory is made. It is set when the capture starts, and cannot be in the future.
help.contract.signed: The generated contract, once signed by every party, as a PDF. It is linked to the contract it signs.
billing.title: Billing
billing.simulateFirst: Run the dry run first to check the amounts.
billing.simulationBody: Amounts computed for this month; nothing is issued yet. Check each lease before issuing the rent calls.
billing.nothingToIssue: No rent call to issue this month: the active leases are already billed, or no lease is active.
billing.noDocumentsAction: Run the dry run, then issue the rent calls.
billing.receiptsNote: Receipts are issued automatically every hour once a rent call is paid in full; a partial payment gives a payment receipt, never a quittance.
billing.issueBody: {n} rent call(s) totalling {total} will be issued, archived and e-mailed to the tenants. An issued document never changes: it can only be cancelled and reissued.
billing.cancelBody: Rent call {number} will be cancelled by a cancelling document, then a new rent call is issued if the lease is still billed for this month. Both documents are archived and sent to the tenant.
billing.reissued: Rent call cancelled and reissued as {number}.
payments.title: Payments
payments.autoMatch: Apply to the oldest rent calls
payments.nothingOpen: No rent call of this lease awaits payment.
payments.overApplied: You apply {amount}, more than the {left} available.
payments.savedMatched: Payment recorded, {amount} applied to rent calls.
payments.receiptsIssued: Receipts issued for the rent calls paid in full.
help.billing.reason: Say why the rent call is cancelled; the reason is printed on the cancelling document sent to the tenant.
help.payment.lease: The active or notice-given lease the payment is for.
help.payment.amount: The amount received, in euros. Proposed: what the lease still owes; change it if the tenant paid something else.
help.payment.paidOn: The day the money was received (transfer value date, cheque cashing date). Proposed: today.
help.payment.method: How the tenant paid. Choose CAF for housing benefit paid straight to the landlord.
help.payment.reference: Optional: the transfer label or cheque number, to find it on the bank statement.
help.payment.autoMatch: The payment is applied to the oldest unpaid rent calls. Untick to apply it yourself afterwards.
help.payment.match: Proposed amounts: oldest rent calls first. Change them to split the payment otherwise; the total cannot exceed the amount to apply.
help.payment.receipts: Receipts are issued every hour; this button issues them now for the rent calls paid in full.
charges.title: Charges
charges.importBody: Drop the CSV file the syndic exports (and the PDF statement if you have it): each row becomes a draft charge, with the recoverable part the syndic states, which you then confirm.
charges.imported: {n} row(s) imported as drafts: check them, then confirm them.
charges.label: Label
charges.locked: This charge is part of an issued reconciliation: it can no longer change. Cancel the reconciliation to correct it.
charges.drafts: {n} imported charge(s) to confirm before the reconciliation.
charges.emptyAction: Add a charge or import the syndic statement.
charges.startBody: A draft reconciliation is created for {asset} over the exercise below; nothing is sent to the tenants yet.
recon.title: Reconciliation
recon.heading: {year} charges reconciliation
recon.chargesBody: The exercise's confirmed charges. Only the recoverable part is shared between tenants, in proportion to their days of occupancy.
recon.allocationBody: Each lease's share in proportion to its days of occupancy over the {days} days of the exercise. Vacant days stay with the landlord.
recon.balancesBody: Provisions collected against each tenant's share. Where the law requires it, a balance is spread over monthly instalments, shown under the balance.
recon.provisionsBody: For each lease: the new monthly provision and how the balance is settled. Each choice is saved at once.
recon.apply: Apply from the next rent call
recon.issueBody: Exactly what will be issued: one RG statement per lease, archived and e-mailed to the tenant.
recon.provisionFrom: Provision raised to {amount} from the next rent call
recon.issueConfirm: {n} reconciliation statement(s) will be issued, archived and sent to the tenants; balances are carried as chosen. An issued statement never changes.
recon.cancelBody: Each statement is cancelled by a cancelling document sent to the tenant; balances not yet carried are removed, carried ones are reversed the next month, and the charges can change again. A provision already applied stays.
help.charge.asset: The property the charge is for.
help.charge.category: The kind of charge; it sets its place in the property income return.
help.charge.label: The syndic's or invoice's label, to find it again.
help.charge.amount: The whole amount of the charge, in euros, as on the statement or invoice.
help.charge.recoverable: The part the tenant must pay back (recoverable charges of décret 87-713). Proposed: €0; for a syndic statement, use its « récupérable » column.
help.charge.chargedOn: The date of the statement or invoice. Proposed: today.
help.charge.exercise: The year of the exercise reconciled; follows the date until you change it.
help.charge.paidOn: Optional: the day you paid it; used for the tax return.
help.import.year: The statement's exercise, usually last year.
help.import.csv: The CSV file exported from the syndic's extranet; it is virus-scanned and archived.
help.import.pdf: The syndic's statement as a PDF; it is attached to every imported row as supporting document.
help.import.chargedOn: The date given to the imported charges. Proposed: the last day of the exercise.
help.import.mapping: The exact column names in the file's first row. The proposed names match the usual syndic export; an empty recoverable cell counts as €0.
help.recon.exercise: The syndic's exercise: from the 1st of a month to the last day of a month. Proposed: the calendar year.
help.recon.provision: The proposed provision covers, month by month, the exercise's recoverable share, rounded up to the euro.
help.recon.newProvision: The new monthly charges provision. Proposed: the exercise's share divided by twelve, rounded up to the euro.
help.recon.settlement: How the balance is settled: carried on the next rent call (spread over instalments where the law requires it), set against the deposit of a tenant who left, or settled directly.
help.recon.settle: Do it once every balance has been carried on the rent calls.
help.recon.reason: Explain the correction; the reason is printed on the cancelling documents.
charge.category.recoverable_utilities: Recoverable charges paid by the landlord
charge.category.owner_expense_charged_to: Landlord expense charged to the tenant
tax.title: {year} property income
tax.intro: {year}'s income and charges, declared in {filing}: micro-foncier and the régime réel side by side, each 2044 line linked to the charges and payments behind it.
tax.issued: Summary issued: the PDF and the CSV are archived.
tax.emptyAction: Click « Compute »: you will be asked to sign in again with strong authentication.
tax.flag.missing_document: {n} charge(s) without a supporting document: they are counted, but keep the invoice or statement in case of an audit.
tax.flag.draft_charge: {n} draft charge(s) are not deducted until confirmed.
tax.flag.unmatched_payment: {n} unmatched payment(s): counted at the date received.
tax.issuedBody: Summary issued under {regime} on {at}; it no longer changes.
tax.lowerNote: The lower taxable base is {regime}'s; the choice is yours, and the régime réel binds you for several years.
tax.furnished: Furnished lettings: {amount} of gross receipts, declared outside the 2044.
tax.noLineMap: This year's 2044 line parameter is missing: the labels cannot be shown.
tax.issueBody: The {year} summary will be issued under {regime}: the RF PDF and the CSV of the lines are archived, and the year is no longer recomputed.
tax.reelLock: Opting for the régime réel binds you for {years} years.
help.tax.stepUp: Computing or issuing the summary needs a recent strong (MFA) sign-in, as for any tax data.
help.tax.micro: Micro-foncier applies a flat allowance to gross rents; it is open only under the income threshold set by law, without furnished lettings or special schemes.
help.tax.reel: The régime réel deducts the charges actually paid; a deficit is set against global income within the legal limit, the rest carried to later years.
help.tax.lines: Click a line to see the charges and payments behind it; in orange, what deserves a look.
docs.title: Documents
docs.name: Document
docs.more: {shown} documents shown of {total}: narrow the filters to see the others.
docs.notCancellable: This rent call no longer stands: it was already cancelled.
docs.exportBody: The ZIP holds every document you may read, with a CSV index (number, type, period, fingerprint). You will be asked for a strong sign-in; the archive is prepared in the background.
docs.exportReady: Archive ready: {n} document(s). The download link is valid for 10 minutes.
params.intro: The legal parameters Tenure uses, each with its effective date and its source. A value is never changed: a new dated value is added.
params.addBody: The value applies from the date given, never before today; earlier values stay in force for their periods. You will be asked for a strong sign-in.
params.badJSON: The value is not valid JSON.
grants.intro: Give read access to your portfolio to a co-owner or your accountant, by their Socrate identifier. An access is revoked, never deleted.
grants.inviteBody: The person will read your portfolio with their own Socrate account; you will be asked for a strong sign-in.
grants.coOwnerHelp: reads the whole portfolio, changes nothing
grants.accountantHelp: reads the financial data, without tenant contact data or guarantors
grants.revokeBody: {sub} loses access to your portfolio at their next request; the access stays listed as revoked. You will be asked for a strong sign-in.
profile.myDataBody: Download your personal data (profile and access given or received) as JSON.
help.docs.number: The number printed on the document, e.g. AL-… for a rent call or QL-… for a receipt.
help.grants.sub: The person's identifier in Socrate, found in their Socrate account.
help.params.from: The first day the value applies; today or later.
help.params.value: The new value as JSON, taken from the value in force to be changed.
help.params.source: The text the value rests on (law, decree, order); it is kept with it.
help.profile.myData: Your right of access (GDPR): a strong sign-in is asked and the export is recorded.
home.todos.none: Nothing to report: no arrears, no blocker, no payment to match.
todo.blocked: {lease}: {n} item(s) to settle before the contract or activation — {first}
amendment.title: Lease amendment
amendment.intro: The amendment is numbered and archived; the change applies to the lease from its effective date, and the next rent call uses it.
amendment.noBox: No box available: create it first in your assets.
help.amendment.kind: An amendment changes a current lease: a rent agreed other than by the annual revision, a new joint tenant, or an extra box. An amendment never changes the deposit.
help.amendment.effectiveOn: The day from which the change applies. It cannot precede the lease start.
help.amendment.tenant: The tenant is added as jointly liable. Pick them among your tenants or create them with the button on the right.
help.amendment.box: A box of your assets that no other current lease rents.
help.amendment.rent: The new monthly rent excluding charges. In a rent-controlled zone it is checked against the zone ceiling on the effective date.
help.amendment.boxRent: The new total rent excluding charges, box included. Leave empty to keep the current rent.
help.amendment.reason: Shown in the amendment, for example « agreement of the parties » or « extra box rented ».
revision.title: Annual rent revision (IRL)
revision.from: First month at the new rent
revision.forfeited: The revision is claimed too long after its anniversary: it is lost and the rent stays the same. The reference index still moves on.
revision.aboveCeiling: The current rent is already above the zone ceiling: it stays the same. Check the agreed rent.
revision.cappedIrl: The increase is limited by the IRL cap in force.
revision.cappedCeiling: The revised rent is limited to the rent-control zone ceiling.
revision.confirm: Applying the revision issues the revision notice to the tenant; months already billed are not billed again.
revision.confirmUnchanged: The rent does not change. Applying the revision records the new reference index and issues the notice.
templates.intro: The templates of the documents Tenure produces, in French, shipped with each release of the application. A change to a template creates a new version: an issued document keeps the version it was produced with and is never generated again.
layout.title: Room layout
layout.denied: The room layout is not available to your role.
layout.empty: This asset has no layout yet. Create it from the template of its kind, then adjust it once: every inventory will start from it.
layout.emptyRead: This asset has no room layout yet.
layout.seed: Create the layout from the template
layout.staleKept: The layout changed in the meantime. Your changes are kept: save them to replace the stored version, or discard them.
help.layout: The layout lists the asset's rooms and their elements, in the order of the visit. Every entry inventory starts from it, and the exit is compared element by element; removing an element does not change the inventories already made.
help.layout.bedrooms: One « Chambre » room is created per bedroom, numbered.
help.layout.furnished: A dwelling let furnished must have the furniture listed by decree: it is added to the rooms concerned.
help.layout.installedOn: Date it was installed or last redone, if you know it: it is used for wear and tear at exit.
review.title: Review and sign
review.reservationsHint: This party's reservations, if any (printed on the document)
review.notSignable: The inventory is signed once its capture is completed.
review.issuedNote: Every party has signed: the inventory is issued.
review.issued: Every party has signed: the inventory is issued.
review.requested: Signature request created: each party signs in turn.
review.inTurn: Each party signs in turn on this tablet. After each signature, come back here and refresh.
review.request.cancelled: The electronic signature request was cancelled.
review.request.refused: The electronic signature request was refused or expired at the provider.
review.emailRequired: An e-mail address is needed to sign electronically.
review.esignHelp: The provider creates one link per party; each signs in turn on the tablet.
review.pickRequired: Tick the parties who signed this copy.
help.review: The inventory is signed by the landlord and each co-tenant. By hand: print the copy to sign, have it signed, then upload the signed copy and tick the parties who signed it. Electronically: each party signs in turn on the tablet. Tenure issues the document at the last signature.
compare.title: Entry and exit compared
compare.flagged: {n} difference(s) to qualify before the deposit is returned.
compare.none: Nothing worse or missing compared with the entry.
inventory.check.exit-item-to-check: Item carried over from the entry, not checked yet
help.capture.keysReturnedOn: The day the tenant returns the keys. It starts the deposit's return deadline; it cannot be in the future.
help.compare: Each exit item against its state at entry, corrected by the accepted completions. A worse or missing item will be qualified (fair wear, ageing, damage) before the deposit is returned.
completion.title: Completions of the entry inventory
completion.noHeating: No heating window: the entry took place during the heating season.
completion.notIssued: The windows run once the entry inventory is issued.
completion.letterHint: Optional: the letter or e-mail received, as a PDF or an image.
completion.pickItem: Pick an item of the entry
completion.commentHint: What the tenant asks to add
completion.lineRequired: At least one item to complete.
completion.askRequired: Give a condition, whether it works, or a comment.
completion.decisionHint: The decision issues the EC completion. The issued entry inventory is not changed: the accepted lines stand as the entry state for the exit.
help.completion: The tenant may ask to complete the entry inventory within ten days, and for the heating during the first month of the heating season (law of 6 July 1989, art. 3-2). Record the request as received, then accept or refuse each line.
help.completionReason: Within ten days after the entry inventory, on any item; during the heating season, on heating items only.
help.asset.collectiveBuilding: Tick when the dwelling is in a building managed by a syndic. At the deposit restitution, a share can then be held back until the building's annual accounts are approved (art. 22 of the law of 6 July 1989).
deposit.noGrid: No grid: a deduction is the whole cost, justified line by line.
deposit.gridSource: Source (collective agreement, agreement of the parties)
deposit.gridRecorded: Grid recorded and annexed to the lease
deposit.waitExit: The restitution is prepared once the exit inventory is issued, with the day the keys were returned.
deposit.nothingFlagged: Nothing worse or missing: no deduction from the inventory.
deposit.shareHint: Tenure computes the tenant's share with the lease's wear grid, from the item's age; without a grid, the whole cost.
deposit.quoteRequired: The quote or invoice is required.
deposit.holdback: Holdback until the accounts are approved
deposit.toReturn: To pay back to the tenant
deposit.issueConfirm: The RD statement is issued and archived; the deductions can no longer change.
deposit.approvalRequired: The approval date of the accounts is required.
deposit.regularisationProof: Attach the proof of the regularisation.
help.deposit: The deposit is paid back within one month of the keys without deduction, two months with; each deduction is backed by a quote or invoice (law of 6 July 1989, art. 22). Past the deadline, 10 % of the rent per started month is owed, unless the tenant gave no new address.
help.deposit.grid: A wear grid, from a collective agreement or agreed by the parties, sets per category the lifetime, franchise, yearly reduction and residual value: the tenant's share allows for normal wear.
help.deposit.approved: In a building under a syndic, a share can be held back until the annual accounts are approved; its balance is due within the following month.
about.apiUnavailable: The server's information is not available.
about.mismatch: The loaded app ({web}) is not the one the server pins ({pinned}): reload the page, or the server serves another bundle.
about.copyFailed: Copy not possible in this browser
home.calendar.none: No deadline in the next 90 days.
calendar.none: No deadline in the coming year.
calendar.denied: The calendar is not available with this role.
calendar.assetHint: The deadlines of the coming year, computed by Tenure from the diagnostics, leases, inventories and deposit. A past deadline still to deal with is flagged overdue.
calendar.kind.diagnostic_expiry: End of validity of the {what} diagnostic
calendar.kind.insurance_certificate: Ask for the home insurance certificate
calendar.kind.completion_ten_day: End of the window to complete the entry inventory
calendar.kind.completion_heating: End of the window to complete the heating
notice.title: Record a notice
notice.reason.new_job_after_loss: New job after a job loss
notice.rel.concubin: Their partner of at least one year
notice.rel.spouse_ascendant: An ascendant of the spouse or partner
notice.rel.spouse_descendant: A descendant of the spouse or partner
notice.protectedLabel: Protected tenant (over 65, resources under the ceiling)?
notice.letterTerms: The notice aims at the lease's end on {end}; the tenant must receive it by {latest} ({months} months before).
notice.letterReady: Notice letter {number} generated: send it, then record its reception.
notice.ends: The lease will end on {end} ({months}-month notice).
notice.warning.tense_zone_not_flagged: The asset is not flagged in a high-demand area: check the town.
notice.saved: Notice recorded: the lease ends on {end}.
help.notice.givenBy: The tenant may give notice at any time; the owner only for the lease's end, on a legal ground, and never on a mobility lease.
help.notice.reason: An unfurnished home has a three-month notice, one month for a ground listed in article 15 of the law of 6 July 1989 or in a high-demand area. A furnished or mobility lease has one month.
help.notice.tenantLetter: The tenant's letter or deed, as a PDF or a photo. It is scanned then archived with the lease.
help.notice.ownerReason: Sale, repossession to live in, or a legitimate and serious ground (article 15 of the law of 6 July 1989).
help.notice.price: A notice to sell is an offer to the tenant at this price for the first two months of the notice.
help.notice.conditions: The sale conditions offered to the tenant, such as cash payment.
help.notice.beneficiary: The person who will live in the home as their main residence.
help.notice.relationship: The beneficiary must be one of the persons the law allows.
help.notice.address: The beneficiary's current address, stated in the letter.
help.notice.grounds: For instance repeated unpaid rent or neighbourhood disturbance, to be proven.
help.notice.protected: A tenant over 65 whose resources are under the ceiling cannot be given notice without a rehousing offer.
help.notice.receivedOn: The notice runs from its reception by the other party, not its sending.
help.notice.delivery: Registered letter with acknowledgement, bailiff's deed, or hand delivery against receipt.
help.notice.sentOn: The letter's sending date, for the record.
help.notice.tracking: The registered letter's number or the deed's reference.
terms.title: Lease terms
terms.nextRenewal: Next tacit renewal on {day}, unless notice is given.
terms.noRenewal: This lease does not renew tacitly.
terms.beyondTerm: This lease, which does not renew, has run past its term with no end date: record its end or a new lease.
vacancy.title: Vacancy
renewal.title: Rent re-evaluation at renewal
renewal.intro: A manifestly under-valued rent may be re-evaluated at the lease's renewal, on a proposal the tenant receives at least six months before the term (loi of 6 July 1989, art. 17-2).
renewal.stepsDue: {n} step(s) due to apply to the rent.
renewal.refusedNote: The rent stays as it is. Failing agreement, either party may refer to the commission départementale de conciliation, then the judge before the lease's term.
renewal.largeAgglomeration: Agglomeration of more than a million inhabitants
renewal.previewText: Renewal on {renewal}, letter to deliver by {latest}. Increase of {increase} ({percent}), in {n} yearly steps.
renewal.reference.incomplete: Each reference needs an address and a rent.
renewal.issued: Letter {number} ready: deliver it to the tenant, with the text of article 17-2.
help.renewal.proposed: The monthly rent excluding charges you propose for the renewed lease. It must exceed the current rent; in a zone tendue, it may not exceed the computed cap.
help.renewal.references: Rents seen over three years for comparable dwellings nearby: at least three, six in an agglomeration of more than a million inhabitants.
help.renewal.largeAgglomeration: Tick if the home is in an agglomeration of more than a million inhabitants (Paris, Lyon, Marseille, Lille…): six references are then needed.
recovery.title: Recovery of unpaid rent
recovery.since: Unpaid since the due day of {day} · {amount} overdue.
recovery.letterReady: Letter {number} ready: send it, then record the sending.
recovery.resolution: The clause résolutoire may take effect from {day}, if the debt is not paid.
recovery.suspended: The payment plan is respected: the escalation is suspended.
recovery.step.insurance_claim: Claim to the insurer (GLI or Visale)
recovery.letterFirst: Prepare the letter first, or upload the one you sent.
plan.title: Payment plan
plan.intro: The plan covers the rent overdue today, {debt}. Its instalments must add up to exactly that; while it is respected, and the current rent paid, the escalation is suspended.
plan.reason.instalment_late: An instalment was not paid in time: the escalation resumes.
plan.reason.current_rent_unpaid: The current rent is unpaid: the escalation resumes.
plan.rowsIncomplete: Each instalment needs a date and an amount.
plan.totalMismatch: The instalments add up to {total}; the debt is {debt}.
help.plan.agreedOn: The day you and the tenant agreed on the plan; it covers the rent overdue that day.
help.plan.count: How many monthly instalments; « Spread evenly » recomputes the amounts.
help.plan.first: The first instalment's date; the next fall on the same day of the following months.
help.recovery.doneOn: The day of the sending, service or claim; it cannot be in the future.
help.recovery.delivery: Registered letter, deed of a commissaire de justice, hand delivery or e-mail.
help.recovery.tracking: The registered letter's number or the deed's reference.
help.recovery.deadline: The claim deadline your insurance policy gives.
help.recovery.file: The letter sent or the deed received (PDF, JPEG or PNG); it is archived with the lease.
help.recovery.note: Anything you want to remember about this step.
bank.title: Bank reconciliation
bank.noAccount: Add a bank account to import its statements.
bank.importBody: Export the statement from your bank as OFX or CSV. A line already imported is not added twice.
bank.fileFormat: Only OFX and CSV statements are read.
bank.ofx: The OFX statement is read as it is.
bank.autoPreview: {n} credit(s) recognised for sure (rent call number, tenant's name, housing allowance); {left} are left for you.
bank.noRentSuggestion: No rent fits; split the line yourself.
bank.noChargeSuggestion: No charge fits; record the charge in the charges ledger first.
bank.splitBody: Split {amount} (« {label} ») across one or more leases: a third party paying, a transfer covering two rents.
bank.splitIncomplete: Each part needs a lease and an amount.
help.bank.file: The file your bank exports; it is scanned, then archived.
help.bank.label: A name to recognise the account, for example « Rent account ».
help.bank.last4: To tell two accounts apart; the full IBAN is never stored.
help.bank.note: Why this line is neither rent nor a charge: a transfer between your accounts, bank fees…
tax.flag.superseded_by_loan: {n} loan charge(s) typed by hand are set aside: the recorded amortisation table already gives line 250.
tax.flagShort.superseded_by_loan: set aside, the loan replaces it
loans.intro: The loans that finance this asset. Each year, the interest and insurance of the instalments go to line 250 of the tax summary by themselves.
loans.empty: No loan recorded for this asset.
loans.label: Label
loans.rateInvalid: A rate between 0 and 99.9999 %, for example 3,45.
loans.firstDueRequired: The first instalment's day is required.
loans.previewInstalment: Monthly instalment of {amount} before insurance, the last one on {last}.
loans.previewTotals: Interest over the whole term: {interest}; insurance: {insurance}.
help.loans.label: The name you will know this loan by, for example « Purchase loan ».
help.loans.principal: The principal borrowed, as the loan offer states it.
help.loans.rate: The offer's nominal annual rate, before insurance. A month's interest is the balance times this rate divided by twelve.
help.loans.firstDue: The day of the first instalment; the next ones fall on the same day of the following months.
help.loans.insurance: The borrower insurance paid with each instalment. It is deductible on line 250, like the interest.
help.loans.table: Copy the bank's table from a spreadsheet or its export: one instalment a line, the day, the principal, the interest and the insurance, separated by tabs or semicolons. Header and total lines are skipped. Use this for a variable rate, a deferral or quarterly instalments.
ledger.title: Journal {year}
ledger.intro: Every movement of money of the year, in double entry on a cash basis: rent received, charges paid, loan instalments, deposits received and returned.
ledger.fecClosedOnly: The FEC is produced only for a closed year, once its tax summary is issued.
ledger.balanceSign: Balance = debit − credit: positive for a use or a claim, negative for a resource or a debt.
help.ledger.closed: A year is closed once its tax summary is issued: its payments, charges and loan instalments can no longer change. Attaching a missing invoice stays possible. The exports need a recent multi-factor sign-in.
dashboard.title: Dashboard {year}
dashboard.compareTitle: Year to date, against last year
dashboard.lower.micro: Micro-foncier is the lower on these figures.
dashboard.lower.reel: The régime réel is the lower on these figures.
dashboard.taxNone: No estimate for {year}: that year's 2044 lines are not published yet.
dashboard.noMonths: This year has not started yet.
dashboard.monthsLegend: Green is money in, grey money out; on the right, the month's balance.
help.dashboard.source: Every figure comes from the owner's journal, on a cash basis: the same as the tax summary's. The yields put the rent and the net over the asset's acquisition price, for a year's worth; during the year, annualised over the days elapsed. The export needs a recent multi-factor sign-in.
help.dashboard.tax: The year's tax summary computed as an indication, not stored, under both regimes. It exists only for a year whose 2044 lines are published.
maintenance.heading: Maintenance and incidents
maintenance.incidentsIntro: Tenants' requests and the works you start, from report to invoice. A repair's invoice becomes a deductible charge; an improvement's is capitalised on the asset.
maintenance.title: Title
maintenance.photoHint: {n} photo(s) attached. PDF, JPEG or PNG.
maintenance.improvementCapitalised: capitalised on the asset, never deducted.
maintenance.contractsIntro: The periodic upkeep of your assets: boiler, chimney, other checks. Each visit recorded sets the next one, which the obligations calendar recalls.
maintenance.intervalRequired: The interval is required for this kind.
help.maintenance.treatment: Repair, upkeep and the improvement of a dwelling are deductible from the rental income (line 224). An improvement brings new equipment or comfort (a fitted kitchen, a more efficient boiler…); on premises that are not a dwelling (a box) it is not deductible. Construction, reconstruction and enlargement never are: they add to the asset's value. When in doubt, ask your accountant.
help.maintenance.interval: For a boiler or a chimney, Tenure applies the rhythm the regulations set; you may choose a shorter interval, never a longer one.
help.maintenance.responsible: The boiler's servicing and the chimney's sweeping fall in principle to the tenant (minor repairs): Tenure reminds you to ask for the certificate. Choose « the landlord » if you took a contract at your own cost.
help.maintenance.firstDue: The day the first visit is due. Then each visit recorded sets the next one.
help.maintenance.certificate: The certificate the contractor gives after the visit. It is kept in the asset's documents.
maintenance.treatmentHint.charge: A « repairs » charge is created: deductible on line 224 of the tax summary, to be matched to the bank debit.
maintenance.treatmentHint.capitalised: No charge is created: the amount is capitalised on the asset, posted to a fixed-asset account in the journal, and never deducted.
maintenance.fuelRequired: The fuel is required for a chimney.
help.maintenance.fuel: The sweeping rhythm depends on the fuel: Tenure applies the one the regulations set. If your département asks for more, choose a shorter interval.
bic.intro: Furnished letting under the réel: the asset's component grid, its furniture and works, and their depreciation. The defaults come from Tenure's legal parameters.
bic.gridSummary: Depreciable basis {basis}, first let furnished on {on}.
bic.proposalHint: Default proposal: check the shares and durations with your accountant, then record it.
bic.inServiceRequired: The day first let furnished is required.
bic.costsExpensed: Expense the acquisition costs in the first year rather than depreciate them
bic.sharesInvalid: The shares must add up to 100 % (now {total}).
bic.label: Label
bic.monthsRequired: The duration of works is required.
bic.expensedLine: Furniture and works expensed this year: {amount}.
bic.resultIntro: The BIC result of your furnished letting, on your shares: the depreciation deducted may not exceed receipts less the other charges; the excess is carried without time limit. Micro-BIC is computed beside.
bic.noFurnished: No asset let furnished this year.
bic.microClosed: The receipts exceed the micro-BIC threshold: only the réel is open.
bic.lower: The more favourable regime this year: {regime}.
bic.issueBody: The year's declaration is issued under {regime}: its figures are kept as they are and the component grids it used are frozen. It can no longer change. A recent strong sign-in is asked for.
help.bic.inService: Depreciation starts on the day first let furnished, not on the purchase.
help.bic.costs: Notary and agency costs: capitalised by default and spread over the components. Expensing them in the first year is an option.
help.bic.components: Land is not depreciated. Each component has its share of the price and its duration; check them with your accountant. A grid a declaration used no longer changes.
help.bic.works: A repair or upkeep is expensed; an improvement or construction is depreciated, whatever its amount.
help.bic.treatment: Tenure applies the rule: the nature first, then for furniture the small-equipment threshold. You may force the other treatment with a reason, kept in the audit trail.
grants.managerHelp: runs the SCI with every right, grants and declarations included
help.loans.sciName: The loan paid for your parts of this SCI: its interest and insurance are deducted with your share, on your own 2044.
sci.sectionBody: An SCI at the income tax has its own portfolio: its assets, its leases, its books. You become its manager.
sci.createHint: Only an SCI at the income tax is supported. A strong sign-in will be asked.
sci.capitalRequired: The number of parts of the capital is required.
sci.partsRequired: The number of parts is a positive integer.
sci.intro2072: The SCI's result, computed with the rules of the 2044 réel, and each associate's share by the parts held on 31 December.
sci.linesNote: The 2072's line numbers wait for your accountant's validation: amounts are given by nature.
sci.issueBody: The result and the shares are stored as they are; no movement of parts can be dated in that year any more. A strong sign-in will be asked.
sci.blocker.year_open: The year is not over: the 2072 is filed after 31 December.
sci.blocker.furnished_receipts: The SCI received furnished rent this year: furnished letting may make it liable to corporate tax. See your accountant; the 2072 is not issued.
sci.blocker.register_incomplete: On 31 December the parts held do not make up the capital: complete the register of associates.
sci.sharesIntro: Your shares of the 2072s issued by the SCIs you are an associate of; your tax summary adds them to your revenus fonciers.
sci.pending: {n} SCI you are an associate of has not issued its 2072 of the year yet: your share is not counted yet.
sci.sharesLineNote: The 2044 line for these amounts waits for your accountant's validation.
help.sci.create: The SCI becomes a portfolio of its own: choose it in the selector at the top to manage its assets, its associates and its 2072.
help.sci.regimeFrom: The day the SCI is taxed at the income tax, usually its creation.
help.sci.capital: The number of parts of the capital; it does not change here (capital increases or reductions are not supported).
help.sci.regime: An SCI under corporate tax is not supported.
help.sci.link: An associate linked to a Tenure person sees their share of the issued 2072s in their own space. You can link yourself, or a person with live access to the SCI.
help.sci.reason: A subscription creates parts within the capital; a transfer, a gift or a succession moves parts held.
help.sci.onDate: The day of the movement: the receiver holds the parts from that day. The year's result is split by the parts held on 31 December.
dashboard.partsLoan: interest of the loan for parts of {sci}: {amount}
dashboard.sciPending: {n} SCI has not issued its 2072 yet: its share is missing.
dashboard.sciScope: An SCI files no 2044: its result goes on the 2072, for its associates.
job.audit.head: Audit trail seal
diag.legalCap: The report states {date}: the shorter legal validity applies.
bic.yearOpen: This year is not over: it is declared after 31 December. The figures above are an estimate to date.
bank.recordedHelp: This credit may be a payment already recorded by hand: link it rather than record it a second time.
bank.linked: Line linked to the payment already recorded.
inventory.steps: Steps: 1. schedule the appointment; 2. start it on site; 3. finish the capture; 4. review and sign. You can fill in the rooms now.
